objective: Equity book v1.2 (simple construction): preregistered after T-20261002-25 passed its mechanical rule. Test whether the T-25 R6 construction (9-theme composite M0/M1, industry-demeaned rank weights, easy-to-borrow shorts, book-level EWMA SPY beta hedge, VIX > 20.60 halving, weekly 5 tranches, fill at the close of t+1) survives an Alpaca Reg T account at $1M -- gross incl. hedge and T-bills <= 1.8x equity, whole shares and the engine minimum order, netted tranches, conservative delisting bound, borrow 0 bp on ETB per Alpaca docs, no interest on cash -- and reaches evaluation-standard v2 tier P1 under a 10-variant DSR family (111-trial program DSR disclosed, < 0.50 caps at P1), with a 100-seed placebo, so that quant1 (F1 neutral, k 0.5 plus T-bill leg) and quant2 (F2 SPY 1.0 plus a 0.3 overlay) can start paper incubation and a forward record from 2026-09-18.

cost_table.judged_cost: cost model v1 at the close snapshot (make_cost_fn("close")): half-spread + square-root impact at E = $1M + fees 0.5 bp per side; borrow 0 bp on easy-to-borrow shorts (Alpaca docs), 25 bp reported; ETF branch for SPY and the T-bill leg
cost_table.two_x_cost_check: 2x trading costs plus borrow 100 bp a year on all short notional (V3 and robustness item a)
cost_table.fixed_comparison: T-25 R6 (8 bp ladder steps and 25 bp borrow) reported as the identity baseline

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly, Malamud and Pedersen (SFI 22-63, 2022 version; RFS 2026): portfolios that put ML return forecasts, risk and trading costs into one objective keep positive out-of-sample net Sharpe ratios, reaching 1.38 for Portfolio-ML for an investor whose wealth reaches $10 billion by 2020, while cost-agnostic Markowitz portfolios fall to negative net returns.
sources.project_applicability: Sets the realistic ceiling for a cost-aware book and supports one optimizer holding alpha, risk and costs (design section 8); M3 (random-feature ridge) follows this line.
sources.reflection: 2022 working-paper version (the RFS 2026 numbers may differ); price-impact costs only; a $10 billion large-cap investor, not a $1M U3000 book; the full model set needs about 75 GB, so we run a reduced version.

sources.core_claim: AQR Alternative Thinking 2023 Issue 4, Exhibit A1 (Hedge Fund Research data, May 1996 - August 2023, net of fees, 87 systematic and 337 discretionary long/short equity funds including dead funds): systematic funds' Sharpe ratio is 0 / 0.2 / 0.51 / 0.87 / 1.18 at the 10th / 25th / median / 75th / 90th percentile, with median beta 0.08.
sources.project_applicability: Calibrates the target: a book net Sharpe of 0.5-1.0 is the professional median to 75th percentile, and K1's 1.19 anchor bar sits at the systematic 90th percentile.
sources.reflection: Manager-written note; fund returns are net of fees while our book has no fees but no institutional execution either; global funds, not US-only; exact publication date not printed in the snapshot.

sources.core_claim: Chen and Velikov (JFQA 58(3), May 2023): after effective bid-ask spreads, post-publication decay and restricting to the post-2005 trading-technology era, the average published anomaly is expected to earn just 4 bp per month net; the strongest anomalies net at best about 10 bp, and several methods for combining anomalies net around 20 bp.
sources.project_applicability: Single anomalies are not worth trading alone after costs; only cost-aware combinations can clear the bar, which is why the book replaces standalone anomaly tests.
sources.reflection: Spread costs only (no impact, no short-sale fees); anomaly portfolios as published; the date is the issue month.

sources.core_claim: Frazzini, Israel and Moskowitz ('Trading Costs', SSRN 3229719, August 2018 draft): on 1.7 trillion dollars of live executions by a large institutional manager across 21 developed equity markets over 19 years, price impact is well approximated by a square-root function of trade size, and actual trading costs are an order of magnitude smaller than previous studies suggest.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the impact term Y * sigma_daily * sqrt(Q/V) with Y = 0.5 in cost model v1 (design section 7) and the small impact at a $1M book.
sources.reflection: Proprietary execution data, not replicable; algorithmic institutional execution, not market-on-open orders at the first print; month-level date.

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen (JF 2023): on a new global data set of 153 factors across 93 countries, most asset pricing factors can be replicated, cluster into 13 themes and work out of sample.
sources.project_applicability: Supports theme-level composites (M0 equal-weights themes) and the theme list of signal library v1.
sources.reflection: Gross factor returns; replication is not net profitability (see Chen-Velikov); the snapshot does not print the issue date.

sources.core_claim: Neuhierl, Randl, Reschenhofer and Zechner (Timing the factor zoo, 2023-03-15 version): over 300 factors and 39 predictors, timing improves almost all factor groups; past factor returns and volatility are the best single predictors; the median timed-vs-untimed improvement is about 2% a year and a timed multifactor portfolio earns about 20% more than its untimed counterpart.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the volatility-state timing variant M0V (gross and ex-ante vol target halved when VIX > 20.60).
sources.reflection: Gross factor returns; PLS aggregation of many predictors does better than any single one; no transaction costs of timing; working-paper version.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca margin and short-selling documentation (fetched 2026-10-02): a Reg T margin account may hold up to 2x equity in marginable securities overnight and receives a margin call the next morning if initial (50%) and maintenance requirements are not met at the end of the day; maintenance is 30% for longs above $6 and the greater of $5.00/share or 30% for shorts at $5 or more; easy-to-borrow shares carry $0 locate and borrow fees for Trading API users while hard-to-borrow shorts need an approved locate; margin interest is 5.00% (elite) or 6.50% (non-elite) on the end-of-day debit balance.
sources.project_applicability: Fixes the account layer of v1.2: total gross including the SPY hedge and the T-bill leg capped at 1.8x equity (Reg T 2x minus a 10% buffer), the Alpaca maintenance table for the end-of-day margin check, borrow 0 bp on easy-to-borrow shorts, debit interest 6.50% a year for F2.
sources.reflection: HTML page without a version date (published_or_updated_at unknown); rates and the ETB fee policy can change; paper accounts may not enforce every rule, so the simulation enforces them itself.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca blog (last updated 2026-09-17): as of 2026-09-22 eligible Trading API users can earn up to 3.56% APY on uninvested USD balances through the High-Yield Cash program, which is only available to users classified as non-pattern day traders.
sources.project_applicability: Sets the cash convention: the main estimate pays no interest on positive cash (paper pays none and it is unverified whether short-sale proceeds count as uninvested cash); a sensitivity credits BIL on positive cash excluding short proceeds; F1 holds a T-bill ETF leg instead of relying on cash interest.
sources.reflection: Marketing blog; rate is variable; does not state whether short-sale proceeds or margin accounts with short positions qualify (to be verified with Alpaca before any live proposal).

hypothesis.statement: H1 (v1.2): the T-25 R6 construction reaches evaluation-standard v2.0.1 tier P1 (no veto; DSR >= 0.70 on the 10-variant family; net placebo percentile >= 0.90; robustness >= 3) for at least one of M0/M1 x U3000/P1000, with zero Reg T margin violations in the F1/F2 account layer at $1M, and the F1 overlay keeps a recent net Sharpe within 0.25 of the strategy level.
hypothesis.failure_mode: Whole shares, the $100 minimum order or the delisting bound cut the recent net Sharpe by more than 0.25; the permutation placebo explains the return (industry-neutral, beta-hedged mechanics); the honest DSR is below 0.70; margin violations at k = 0.5.
hypothesis.measurement: See hypotheses.md section 5: strategy-level R6 (identity to T-25) for DSR, placebo, signal t, robustness and vetoes; account-level F1/F2 replay 2017-10..2026-09 with whole shares, engine rules, Alpaca margin table, cash and delisting conventions for V2 and the economics; diagnostics: factor-ETF spanning and style/specific attribution.
hypothesis.stop_pivot: No P1 variant: the book line pauses until a new signal is admitted under a new contract; no tuning. A P1 variant: paper on quant1 (F1) and quant2 (F2) once the live data parity, the production target parity and two clean dry-run sessions pass; live only after P2, 20 paper sessions and execution acceptance, by the owner.
